# GitHub automation

- Read `docs/RELEASING.md` before changing release workflows. Workflow definitions do not authorize dispatch, publication, repository settings, merges or visibility changes.
- `release-pr.yml` only proposes version/changelog changes through Changesets v3/action v2. It never publishes. Its separate read-only job validates the generated PR without waiting for approval of ordinary PR workflows, which GitHub requires for `GITHUB_TOKEN`-created PRs. Check that job and the required `verify`/`scan` contexts before merging; a bot PR is not an automatic gate waiver.
- `publish.yml` stages only; `finalize-release.yml` only completes GitHub metadata after npm approvals. Both are manual-only, owner/main-only and off unless `NPM_PUBLISH_ENABLED` is exactly `true`. Keep exact commit/origin/main checks and their shared non-canceling concurrency group. Ordinary pushes/PRs/refs must never upload or finalize packages.
- Only `jordan-a-young` may dispatch or rerun finalization; staging reruns are blocked, and a new staging dispatch must reject unreconciled prior staging even when main has advanced. Staging and finalization writes use protected `npm-publish`: main only, owner approval, no admin bypass. Each npm publisher must bind `publish.yml` and that environment, with stage-only permission. Self-approval is owner confirmation, not independent review. Never automate npm approval or grant direct publish/dist-tag permissions incidentally.
- Only the stage job gets `id-token: write`, with read-only contents/Actions access and no npm token. Verify/build/test/scan/pack in the read-only job, then stage only its exact same-run artifact ID and SHA-512-checked tarballs. No rebuilds/tests/install scripts/caches inside the upload job. Keep attempt-qualified artifact names and retain uncertain-upload receipts with `always()`.
- Finalization has no OIDC or npm credentials. Its read-only job authenticates the exact source run/attempt/workflow/actors/main SHA/successful verification job and immutable artifact ID. Require explicit failed-stage reconciliation, not automatic acceptance of failed runs. The write job rechecks provenance, all artifact/registry hashes and current main before tags/releases; never execute files from downloaded artifacts, move conflicting tags, or substitute rebuilt archives. Missing/expired/ambiguous artifacts and incomplete history fail closed.
- Checkout credentials stay disabled. Pass `GITHUB_TOKEN` explicitly to scripts; use command-scoped Git environment for origin synchronization and HTTPS headers for GitHub metadata APIs, never persisted auth config, token-bearing command arguments or logs. Changesets remains the version/changelog engine. Verification binds each version's metadata target; finalization preserves historical targets and rejects later tag moves. Do not generate local tags at HEAD; per-package verified-SHA GitHub completion is idempotent and must not upload to npm. Prior-release reconciliation checks exact Git versions and ancestral matching tags, not all five tags at each newer SHA; see the runbook's trust limits.
- Pin new actions by reviewed immutable commit SHA. Changesets CLI/action major versions must remain compatible. Root/apps remain private; only the five explicit library packages are releasable.
- Bootstrap npm ownership/trusted publishers and verify stage-only permissions separately with owner approval. Staging is still an external write requiring separate authorization; npm approval requires the owner's interactive authentication and 2FA. Trusted publishing does not give provenance to private-source repositories. Never add credentials to repository files or logs.
- Changes to publishing/authentication boundaries require isolated nonpublishing tests and an independent final review. Never test these workflows by actually publishing or creating remote tags/releases without explicit authorization.
